ANALYZER CONTRACT (format_version 1)

The utility is Python standard-library-only, offline and inventory-only.
No formula export switch exists: names, captions, labels, source paths/filenames,
arbitrary connector attributes, SQL text, parameter values, URLs, expressions,
embedded data and archive resource contents are deliberately not exported.
This is minimization by an output allowlist, not a regex-based secret scrubber.
Only fixed enumerations, generated IDs, structural locators, bounded integers,
counts and booleans are emitted. The inventory still reveals report structure;
treat it as potentially business-confidential.

INPUT
  .twb: UTF-8 (BOM allowed), unnamespaced XML, root workbook.
  .twbx: bounded ZIP, exactly one .twb unless --member chooses an exact path.
  Unsupported: UTF-16/other encodings, namespaced elements, DTD/entity declarations,
  encrypted/patched ZIP entries, ZIP64/multi-disk archives, BZIP2/LZMA ZIP
  compression, malformed XML/ZIP, special
  archive files, ambiguous paths. Do not rename rejected inputs to bypass checks.

DEFAULT BOUNDS (scripts/analyze_tableau.py)
  XML/workbook: 16 MiB; archive bytes: 64 MiB; archive members: 512.
  Per member declared size: 32 MiB; total declared uncompressed size: 256 MiB.
  Maximum declared expansion ratio per member: 100:1.
  XML elements: 100,000; element nesting: 64; attributes per element: 64.
  Attribute value: 65,536 characters; all other text bounded by XML byte limit.
  ZIP payload read is bounded independently of declared member size.
  All member metadata is checked, including ignored extracts/resources.
  No member is extracted, no hyperlink is opened, no data/SQL/formula is executed.
  No cache, credentials, network client, binary parser or third-party converter.

The archive is read into a bounded memory buffer; its central-directory byte
records and claimed/actual member counts are checked BEFORE ZipFile allocates
member metadata. Strict central-directory/end-record layout is required
(unsupported trailers or central-directory extensions are rejected). The XML is
UTF-8 decoded before DTD/entity detection; forbidden declarations are rejected
even inside comments as a conservative policy. ElementTree never processes
external resources. Streaming XML events enforce structural limits before
inventory traversal. These are application-level bounds, not an OS sandbox.
Only the selected workbook payload is decompressed/CRC-checked. Ignored archive
payload integrity is not asserted; archive metadata checks are not a complete
ZIP forensic validator. Filesystems may not enforce requested POSIX 0700/0600
modes (notably Windows mounts); use appropriate OS ACLs and an authorized folder.

OUTPUT
  inventory.json
    Source format, XML element count, generated objects and feature occurrences.
    datasource: connector class allowlist, parameter-container hint.
    field: whitelisted datatype/role/type, calc presence and heuristic flags.
    worksheet: declared datasource-dependency references, fields, mark types,
               row/column shelf presence and filter count.
    dashboard: integer size hints; zone objects with bounds and worksheet IDs.
    action: presence-only object, not executable action metadata.
    Unknown enumerated values become "unknown"; bad/missing bounds become null.
    All such cases remain review_needed. No inferred compatibility guarantee.
  compatibility.json
    Inventory status, ALL objects mapped to null target and review_needed,
    unassessed confidence, detected feature keys, explicit limitations and
    separate validation results. All Power BI validation starts not_run.

Object IDs use kind plus document-order ordinal, e.g. field_0001.
Locators are structural paths, e.g. /workbook/*[1]/*[2]/*[3]: the n-th
element child at each step (XML comments/PIs excluded). Read locally against
the SAME input XML; never interpret captions as IDs. Reordering source XML can
change IDs. Dependency and dashboard references retain arrays to expose duplicate
source names rather than selecting the first match. Candidate arrays are capped
at 32 with explicit candidate counts and truncation flags to prevent quadratic
output expansion. Fields beneath an unresolved datasource are not expanded
(candidate_count null and datasource_unresolved true). Every source object is
still inventoried; this bound only limits duplicated reference lists.
A dependency with no mapped
field or an unresolved zone is not an approved omission.

The utility recognizes top-level datasource column definitions and the usual
worksheets/dashboard containers. It does not recover a full Tableau semantic
model, physical/logical relationship graph, field-instance expressions, sorts,
aliases, encodings, titles, formatting, nesting semantics, context filters,
calculation dependencies, or action behavior. A successful empty inventory can
simply mean the input has no supported object containers.
LOD/table-calc detection is lexical, may match quoted text, and misses unsupported
functions/syntax. Feature counts can include duplicated worksheet declarations
or multiple representations. Absence of a flag is never proof of compatibility.
Unknown top-level sections are counted, not silently called migrated; nested
unrecognized constructs require source inspection too.

EXIT AND PERSISTENCE
  0: JSON inventory written; NO conversion or Desktop validation performed.
  2: expected input/security/IO error; generic safe message, no XML parser text.
  Invalid command-line syntax also returns argparse's exit 2.
  Output directory must be NEW and its parent must exist. Never overwrites.
  No output directory is created on analysis failure. An IO failure during
  writing can leave partial files; treat that directory as failed, inspect
  permissions, remove only your own failed artifact, and retry to a NEW path.
  JSON has sorted keys, no clock/user/machine paths, deterministic document order.
  TWBX and TWB inventories differ in source_format; archive order is not preserved.
